clue.text: Pitiful spades, coated in powder on the outside

indicators.note: the powdery word sits on the outside, wrapped round the suit letter

parts.note: something mealy is covered in a fine floury powder
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A sorry hand of spades turns up dusted with powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coated in powder' reads as one adjective, mealy, and 'on the outside' tells you it wraps round the suit letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means miserably small or paltry, so a measly sum is a pitiful one.

clue.text: Rationale of one very involved in scrap

indicators.note: the numeral and abbreviation are wrapped up inside the word for a scrap

parts.note: a mote is a tiny speck or scrap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they got very caught up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, but here it is a tiny fragment, a mote.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason behind an action, its underlying justification.

clue.text: Effect of painkillers taken from sale again

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the phrase and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Pain relief bought again at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' rearranges the nine letters of SALE AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for the absence of pain sensation that pain-relieving drugs produce.

clue.text: Misleading information about new mature stock

indicators.note: the lie goes around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a lie is information intended to mislead
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Fake news is circulating about some fresh livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' here means ancestry, not farm animals or shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of descent or ancestry: someone of good stock has a fine family line.

clue.text: Hindu festival branch virtually covering everything

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the final letter of the branch word is dropped

parts.note: a stick is a small branch

explanation.surface: A Hindu celebration branches out to include practically everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims the last letter of STICK to give STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A holistic approach treats the whole system rather than isolated parts, so it takes in all aspects.

clue.text: Cricket ground agreement seeing loss of front half

indicators.note: losing the front half of the eight-letter agreement word keeps only its back four letters

parts.note: approval is assent or agreement

explanation.surface: A deal over a cricket venue falls half through.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground; dropping APPR from APPROVAL leaves OVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington, south London, is a Test match venue, home of Surrey.

clue.text: Eighty per cent of Independent articles identifying state

indicators.note: four letters out of five are kept, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an indie is an independent company, record label or film
AN and A are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A newspaper's articles spell out the state of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' looks like the British newspaper but means INDIE; 80% of its five letters is INDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Restaurant carrying European feast

indicators.note: the restaurant word holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: An eatery puts on a lavish European banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special delight, and to feast on something is to treat oneself to it.

clue.text: Military activity affected delegate after ship's sailed

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated in manner

indicators.note: the ship letters have sailed off, leaving the delegate word without them

parts.note: to assign a task is to delegate it
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A delegate is rattled once the ship has left port during a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like an anagram signal but is the synonym CAMP; ASSIGN without SS gives AIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a connected series of military operations in a war.

clue.text: A lot of rubbish about popular aims

indicators.note: the shortened rubbish word goes around the popular word
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: trash is rubbish
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Much of the garbage surrounds the people's goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aims' is a verb: one trains a gun on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a weapon or camera on something is to point it at the target.

clue.text: Speculate hydro project is riven by unknown fear mostly

indicators.note: the barrier word is split apart with the other letters inserted

parts.note: a dam is built for hydroelectric power
Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: dread is fear

explanation.surface: A dam scheme is torn apart by vague anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown' is the algebraic Y, a crossword convention; 'is riven by' says the barrier word is split to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to indulge in idle fanciful musing, a loose sense of speculating.

clue.text: End to serenity after old woman brought in floor cleaner, going all over the place

indicators.note: the end letter comes after the rest
the old woman is taken inside the cleaner word

parts.note: a vac is a vacuum cleaner
gran, a grandmother, is an old woman

indicators.note: the last letter of serenity is taken

explanation.surface: Granny takes the hoover out, and calm ends in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagrancy is the state of wandering homeless from place to place.

clue.text: One seizes highest point (hill)

parts.note: the cap is the top or summit
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone grabs the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is a person who takes and holds another prisoner.

clue.text: Woman with many lovers using no soft mystic phrase

indicators.note: the letter for soft is dropped

parts.note: a mantrap is a seductive woman who ensnares men
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A femme fatale gives up gentleness for a spiritual chant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or sound repeated in meditation.

clue.text: Look to Italy to embrace feminine

indicators.note: the letters for feminine are hugged inside the rest

parts.note: a door pushed to is shut
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A glance towards Italy to welcome womanhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' means closed, as in 'pull the door to'. SHUFTI is British army slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a shufti means having a quick glance, from Arabic via soldiers' slang.

clue.text: Loss of coats? That woman records court case

parts.note: she refers to that woman
EPs are extended-play records
a hearing is a session of a court case

explanation.surface: A woman notes a lawsuit over missing overcoats.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'coats' are fleeces; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing strips a sheep of its fleece, so the animals lose their woolly coats.

clue.text: Struggling University athlete putting University first after opening

indicators.note: the moved word follows the opening

parts.note: an intro is an opening section

indicators.note: the U for university is moved to the front of the sportsperson word

parts.note: a Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson who has represented the university

explanation.surface: A college sportsman flounders after a debut, ranking studies first.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sporting honour at Oxford or Cambridge; moving U to the front of BLUE makes UBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble means facing difficulty, having a hard time of it.

clue.text: Lack of faith in a job, say, after poor treatment

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: the word say is knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses faith in their job after being badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the abandonment of a religious belief, a renunciation of faith.

clue.text: I imply nothing will get you healthy again

definitions.text: I imply nothing will get you healthy again

parts.words: I imply nothing will get you healthy again
parts.note: a dummy pill contains nothing, yet the patient's belief that it works makes them feel better

explanation.surface: A pessimist claims there is no cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as gloom, but the speaker is the phenomenon itself: 'nothing' (an inert pill) can make you well.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the improvement in a patient's condition produced by an inactive treatment they believe is real.

clue.text: Song, musical work the writer picked up in shops

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
op is opus, a numbered musical work
the writer refers to me, the setter

explanation.surface: A song and musical piece by me is heard in stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' tempts as a sound signal, but in a down entry it lifts the letters, giving EMPORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store or trading place.

clue.text: Question: who in France blocks old English monarch (though not at first)?

indicators.note: the French word sits inside, blocking the shortened name
the first letter of the king's name is removed

parts.note: Henry was the name of eight English kings
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A query over which French person thwarted a king of old.
explanation.definitionFit: An enquiry is a question asked or a formal investigation.

clue.text: Latin hymn, dreary stuff I translated to English

indicators.note: the letter I is converted into the English abbreviation

parts.note: tedium is dreary boredom

explanation.surface: A dull Latin hymn put into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is an early Christian hymn of praise, opening 'Te Deum laudamus'.

clue.text: Burns, say, nothing less, penning opening text

indicators.note: the shortened word encloses the opening, like a pen holding animals
the nothing letter is taken out

parts.note: Robert Burns was a Scot, the national poet of Scotland
O looks like zero, nothing
a rip is a tear or opening

explanation.surface: The poet Burns, writing nothing, starts on a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like 'the start of', but it is a split, RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a play, film or broadcast.

clue.text: Transmit Republican farewell to Spain, but not in its entirety

indicators.note: the farewell word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye

explanation.surface: A Republican partly says goodbye to Spain over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio a message is to send it by wireless signal.

clue.text: One of some erroneous statements, some quite cut down, mangled

indicators.note: the letters are mashed into a new order
the word quite is shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: Some quotes are quite wrongly abbreviated and garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' makes QUIT; with SOME, 'mangled' reorders the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A misquote is a quotation rendered inaccurately, one item among faulty citations.

clue.text: Fool to throw out stone and taunt

indicators.note: the stone letters are ejected from the fool word

parts.note: a jester is a court fool
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A clown hurls a rock and mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or scoff at someone rudely.

clue.text: Civic dignitary, ditching man, longing to go round island

indicators.note: the man part is dropped from the dignitary

parts.note: an alderman is a senior member of a town council
taken as written

indicators.note: the longing word turns round, read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A councillor, shedding a partner, yearns for an island tour.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERNEY is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is the third-largest of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy.

clue.text: Doctor engaged in weary tone

indicators.note: the doctor letters are placed inside

parts.note: to tire is to grow weary
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor is busy speaking in a weary voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive quality or colour of a sound or voice.

clue.text: Farmers wanting Queen to tour Arab country in a couple of years

indicators.note: the royal tour sits within the pair of year letters

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two years give two Ys

indicators.note: the Queen letters go round the country

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Farmers are without a Queen visiting an Arab land in two years' time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like a deletion signal but is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were historically the class of small freeholding farmers.

clue.text: School of Aristotle rubbished my clue

indicators.note: the words are trashed and their letters scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter complains their clue was panned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyceum was the Athenian gymnasium where Aristotle taught, giving its name to his Peripatetic school.
